goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The custom message length light-theme branch changes from primary lightness 70% to 30%, reversing its existing contrast outside dark themes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in mobile/modal.scss line 102 that the color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme branch (first argument to dark-light-choose) changed from 70% lightness to 30% lightness, which is a significant contrast reversal. This appears to be an error since all other similar changes in the diff maintain the same lightness value for the light theme and only add the dark theme alternative. For example, most changes go from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` - keeping the light theme value the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The mobile topic-card heading changes from primary lightness 20% to 50% in light themes, which is unrelated to choosing secondary for dark themes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the light theme value changed from 20% lightness to 50% lightness, which is a significant change in appearance for light themes. This appears to be an unintended side effect - the PR is about dark theme support, but this change also modifies the light theme behavior from 20% to 50% lightness, making the heading significantly lighter in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — The light-theme name color changed from primary lightness 30% to 50%, regressing this user-card state instead of only adding a dark-theme branch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss line 522, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme value changed from 30% lightness to 50% lightness. This is inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the diff where the light-theme value is preserved (e.g., line 519 in the same file shows `.name` going from 30% to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)` - wait, that's also 30% to 50%. Looking more carefully at line 519-522, both .name and .title had different original values (30% and 50% respectively) but now both use 50%. The finding is correct that the light-theme branch changed from 30% to 50%, which appears to be an unintended regression rather than just adding dark-theme support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The light-theme message-length color changed from primary lightness 70% to 30%, reversing the existing visual intensity.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The finding correctly identifies that for light themes (the first argument to dark-light-choose), the lightness changed from 70% to 30%. This is inconsistent with the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff, where light-theme values typically maintain similar lightness levels and dark-theme values use complementary lightness (e.g., 50%/50%, 40%/60%, 30%/70%). The 30%/70% pattern here appears to be inverted compared to what was intended - it should likely be 70%/30% to maintain the original light-theme appearance while adding dark-theme support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The light-theme star-title color changed from primary lightness 20% to 50%, losing the original emphasis.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the h3 selector shows: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` replacing `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme value changed from 20% lightness to 50% lightness. This is a functional change that reduces emphasis/contrast for the h3 element in light themes, which appears to be an unintended inconsistency compared to other similar changes in the diff that maintain the original light-theme values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:179 — No light- and dark-theme rendering regression test covers this broad color migration, allowing changed light-mode lightness values to ship unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a 'changed light-mode lightness values' issue at line 179, but examining the diff at that line shows the change from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-mode value did change from 20% to 50%, but this is intentional as part of the dark-mode support migration. The finding is essentially a generic request for regression tests rather than identifying a specific bug. The diff shows a consistent pattern of adding dark-light-choose() wrappers across many files, and requesting tests for every CSS color change is not a specific, actionable code review issue grounded in a defect.
